summary.oneLiner: One of India's leading cement manufacturers, headquartered in Hyderabad, with an installed capacity of 10.50 MTPA across six manufacturing facilities spanning Southern, Central and Eastern India.
summary.business: Sagar Cements Limited manufactures and sells clinker and cement — Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC), Portland Pozzolana Cement (PPC) and Portland Slag Cement (PSC) — along with contract manufacturing of Ground Granulated Blast-furnace Slag (GGBS), serving dealers, government departments, institutional builders, real-estate developers, infrastructure companies and retail/captive customers across 13 Indian states. currentContext.strengths: Diversified regional presence with six manufacturing facilities strategically positioned from Southern India to Central and Eastern India, backed by a strong distribution/dealer network (3,368 dealers, 7,423 sub-dealers, 85 warehouses).|Significant captive and green power capacity (108.98 MW total captive power, including 36 MW green power from solar, hydro and waste-heat-recovery systems), reducing dependence on grid power.|Sustainability-linked product differentiation via a GreenPro-certified blended-cement portfolio (PPC, PSC, GGBS) and disciplined use of alternative fuels and raw materials.|Disciplined, phased capacity-expansion approach ('double cement capacity every 10 years') combined with a stringent focus on product quality.
currentContext.strategies: Boosting growth momentum (S1): calibrated capacity expansion strategy aiming to double cement capacity every 10 years, with selective capacity augmentation and operational-efficiency improvements at existing plants.|Building a resilient model (S2): shaping an agile, resilient operating model via process optimisation, fuel/freight cost optimisation, plant utilisation improvements and digital monitoring/manufacturing-technology investments.|Integrating ESG into core operations (S3): aligning growth strategy with the ESG Vision 2030 roadmap.|Strengthening market and product mix: increasing the share of blended cement (~65-68% packed sales / trade mix) and deepening route-to-market strategy to enhance realisations.|Disciplined capital allocation: prioritising high-return brownfield expansions and debottlenecking projects with faster payback, while maintaining prudent leverage and improving EBITDA per tonne.
currentContext.expansion: SGC is expanding cement grinding capacity at its Dachepalli (Andhra Pradesh) plant by 0.75 MTPA via a new cement grinding mill, raising capacity from 2.25 MTPA to 3.00 MTPA, and at its Jeerabad (Madhya Pradesh) grinding unit by 0.50 MTPA to 1.5 MTPA — both targeted by FY2027 — alongside a 4.35 MW Waste Heat Recovery System (WHRS) currently under installation at Gudipadu. During FY2026 the company commissioned a new 6-stage preheater at Dachepalli (completed 117 days ahead of schedule), which raised clinker production by 0.46 MTPA, and commissioned a 6 MW solar power plant at Dachepalli, taking total green/solar power capacity to 36 MW. Further capacity augmentation is planned at the Bayyavaram and Jajpur plants, and the company is evaluating additional on-site/off-site solar power capacity for its remaining plants; a pneumatic AFR feeding system was also commissioned at Jeerabad to expand alternate-fuel usage. Capex strategy remains focused on high-return brownfield expansions and debottlenecking initiatives rather than greenfield capacity.

risks.risk: Commodity price risk - coal and pet coke
risks.note: Coal and Pet Coke, which are close to 36% of cost of production, are priced by external/global markets beyond the Company's control; sharp fluctuations create significant business challenges and can materially impact profitability. Captive limestone mines mitigate raw-material risk but energy/fuel cost exposure remains largely unhedged.

India Ratings & Research revised the Company's long-term rating down from IND A/Negative to IND BBB+/Negative, and its short-term/non-fund-based rating from IND A1 to IND A2, between March 2025 and March 2026, signalling rising financial-risk perception.

risks.risk: Thin bottom-line despite volume and EBITDA growth
risks.note: Despite double-digit revenue growth and a sharp rise in EBITDA during the year, PAT remained near breakeven, underscoring elevated interest/depreciation burden and limited earnings cushion against cost or demand shocks.

one-line thesis: Sagar Cements posted flattish EBITDA (₹38cr) despite 8% volume growth due to high costs at Andhra Cements, but guided for a sharp Q4 recovery to ₹500-550/tonne EBITDA driven by price hikes and Andhra's breakeven. The strategic pivot focuses on retiring debt via ₹350cr Vizag land monetisation over 18 months rather than immediate capex expansion.

One-offs: High depreciation from new CapEx capitalization; No incentives accrued in Q3.
guidance: Volume: 6.0 Mn tonnes for FY26 (9% growth), 7.0 Mn tonnes for FY27; EBITDA/tonne: ₹500-525 for FY26, ₹500-550 for Q4FY26; Capex: ₹489cr (FY26), ₹291cr (FY27).

growth verticals / optionality: Jeerabad expansion (1.0 to 1.5 Mn tonnes) by Q1 FY27; Dachepalli capacity addition by Aug 2026; Long-term target of 12-15 Mn tonnes with major CapEx starting FY29.
margins & cost dynamics: Q3 Power & Fuel: ₹1,408/tonne (down from ₹1,456); Freight: ₹830/tonne. Q4 Cost Savings expected: WHRS at Gudipadu (₹100-125/tonne saving), Jeerabad grinding mill (₹150-200/tonne fixed cost leverage), Andhra electrical efficiency (₹25-50/tonne). Fuel price outlook: Flat for FY26, +2-3% for FY27.
capex / expansion: FY26: ₹489cr (₹303cr done in 9M, ₹186cr budgeted for Q4); FY27: ₹291cr. Key projects: 6-stage preheater at Dachepalli (commissioned), 4.35MW WHRS at Gudipadu (by FY26 end), Jeerabad expansion.
capital allocation: Priority: Debt reduction. Vizag land monetisation expected to yield ~₹350cr net over next 18 months (5-6 tranches). Target D/E ratio to improve to ~0.5x in 18-24 months. No major M&A or greenfield CapEx planned until FY29.
risks & watch-items: Delay in Vizag land policy approval; Volatility in pet coke/domestic coal prices; Competitive pressure from UltraTech (Line-4) and Ramco (Kolimigundla Line-2) capacity additions in AP; Sustained low utilization at Jajpur and Dachepalli plants.
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; Focused on operational efficiency and balance sheet repair; Transparent about Andhra Cements' cost gaps but confident in imminent breakeven.
non-obvious takeaways: Depreciation spike is due to capitalization of completed CapEx (preheater/WHRS) rather than accounting policy change; Fuel cost variance in presentations due to 'as-fired' basis shift highlighting Singareni coal usage at Mattampally vs. imported coal elsewhere.

themes.title: Cement demand & pricing recovery
themes.need: Q1FY27 turned cement from a pricing story into a volume-share-plus-fuel-cost story. ULTRACEMCO grew domestic grey volume +13.1% YoY against an estimated ~7-8% industry, delivered its first Rs 5,000cr+ April-June EBITDA (Rs 5,146cr) with EBITDA/ton held above Rs 1,200, and crossed 200.1 MT domestic capacity a year early - but guided Q2FY27 cost UP ~Rs 130-140/ton and pinned the Rs 1,400/ton consolidated target to Q4FY28. The fuel shock, not price, is the swing factor: JKCEMENT's EBITDA/ton fell to Rs 982 from Rs 1,229 YoY despite +19% grey volume, DALBHARAT flagged pet coke 'surged to nearly $160/t' versus a pre-war $110-115, and NUVOCO defended INR 1,079/ton EBITDA only by cutting petcoke from 37% to 27% of fuel mix in a single quarter. Consolidation is visibly compounding (INDIACEM EBITDA/ton Rs 386->400->509->603 across four quarters; DALBHARAT closed Jaypee at Rs 2,850cr EV with Chunar operational and Rewa on trial within 50 days) even as DALBHARAT slipped its 75mt milestone from FY27 to FY28. SHREECEM/RAMCOCEM/JKLAKSHMI/JSWCEMENT/STARCEMENT/BIRLACORPN ride the same volume + consolidation axis.
themes.driver: Q2FY27 is the guided cost trough - ULTRACEMCO ~Rs 130-140/ton, JKCEMENT ~Rs 150/ton and BIRLACORPN Rs 70-80/ton of incremental cost; then fuel-mix agility (NUVOCO's petcoke swing) and whether DALBHARAT's ~Rs 150/t of procurement savings is really 'permanent, not timing'.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Cement production in India is expected to grow at ~9% in FY2026 (from ~453 MT in FY2025), supported by sustained government investment in infrastructure and steady momentum in real estate.
- Government of India's infrastructure push, including a ~Rs12.2 Lakh Crore infrastructure allocation in the Union Budget 2026-27, is expected to be a key structural demand driver for cement.
- Rapid urbanisation and rising housing demand (including PMAY-U and Smart Cities Mission projects) are cited as tailwinds for cement consumption in urban and peri-urban markets.
- India's real estate sector is expected to grow its contribution to GDP, supporting long-term cement demand; Tier II/III cities cited as an emerging growth pocket.
- India's per-capita cement consumption (~290 kg) remains well below the global average (~540 kg), indicating structural headroom for demand growth.
- PLI scheme and China+1 manufacturing strategy are expected to drive industrial/logistics infrastructure investment and associated cement demand.
- Near-term cost pressure flagged from geopolitical tensions driving sharp increases in pet coke and packaging costs, though management expects structurally strong, scaled, efficient players to be better placed to navigate this.

During FY2026 the company commissioned a new 6-stage preheater at Dachepalli (completed 117 days ahead of schedule), which raised clinker production by 0.46 MTPA, and commissioned a 6 MW solar power plant at Dachepalli, taking total green/solar power capacity to 36 MW. Further capacity augmentation is planned at the Bayyavaram and Jajpur plants, and the company is evaluating additional on-site/off-site solar power capacity for its remaining plants; a pneumatic AFR feeding system was also commissioned at Jeerabad to expand alternate-fuel usage. Capex strategy remains focused on high-return brownfield expansions and debottlenecking initiatives rather than greenfield capacity.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Diversified regional presence with six manufacturing facilities strategically positioned from Southern India to Central and Eastern India, backed by a strong distribution/dealer network (3,368 dealers, 7,423 sub-dealers, 85 warehouses).
- Significant captive and green power capacity (108.98 MW total captive power, including 36 MW green power from solar, hydro and waste-heat-recovery systems), reducing dependence on grid power.
- Sustainability-linked product differentiation via a GreenPro-certified blended-cement portfolio (PPC, PSC, GGBS) and disciplined use of alternative fuels and raw materials.
- Disciplined, phased capacity-expansion approach ('double cement capacity every 10 years') combined with a stringent focus on product quality.
